thread:
maria: Hey team — customer on Dedicated (vpc-edge-2) started seeing 403s from our API after we migrated their LB yesterday. They say it was fine before. Error from backend is 'missing tenant claim'. Repro steps below. Anyone seen this?

Ajay: Can you paste the exact curl you used and the Authorization header (redact tokens)?

maria: Sure — minimal repro hitting their dedicated ingress (IP removed):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED.JWT.TOKEN' \
  'https://34.182.xx.yy/v1/generate' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response: 403 with body: `\{\"error\":\"missing tenant claim\"}`.

kevin: Do we have an ext-authz in front of the runtime for that deployment? Could be header mangling. What do tcpdumps show when you hit the runtime directly?

maria: I SSH'ed into the app host and tcpdump'd on the envoy-facing interface. Here's the request line (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: internal-runtime:8080
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED.JWT.TOKEN, session=eyJhbGciOi...; Path=/; HttpOnly
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 87
```
Notice the Authorization header has our token followed by ", session=..." appended. That would definitely break JWT parsing. We didn't attach any cookie in the client curl.

Ajay: Whoa. So the Authorization header arriving at the runtime contains the session cookie appended with a comma. That smells like a template expansion on the edge proxy that concatenates $http_authorization and $cookie_session or similar. Is this the new edge-auth-proxy image we rolled out?

deploy-bot: edge-auth-proxy deployment v1.4.3 rolled to vpc-edge-2 at 2025-11-08T22:11:03Z by deploy/rollout-batch-17.

kevin: Confirmed. There was a config tweak in v1.4.3 to "simplify header forwarding" so we didn't add more headers (intention: reduce header duplication). Looks like a buggy template in the nginx/HAProxy layer concatenates rather than setting separate headers when both auth and cookie exist.

maria: Repro steps to see the bad behavior locally (customer was able to reproduce):
1) Start a minimal http server that dumps headers: `python -m http.server --bind 0.0.0.0 8080` and wrap with our edge-auth-proxy config.
2) `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED.JWT.TOKEN' --cookie 'session=eyJhbGci...' https://<edge-ip>/dump`
3) Observe header at backend shows `Authorization: Bearer REDACTED.JWT.TOKEN, session=eyJ...`

kevin: That concatenation explains the missing tenant claim — the JWT parser sees the extra bytes after the token and rejects it. Two action items: rollback the header-template change and add a unit/integration test to ensure Authorization is forwarded exactly as received.

Ajay: Can we patch customer infra quickly? Maybe add an envoy filter to strip anything after the first whitespace in Authorization header (quickfix) until we have a proper rollback?

sre-oncall: Quick note: adding a brittle filter risks mishandling legitimate multi-value auth headers. Prefer rollback to proven image. Rolling back on vpc-edge-2 now would be fastest.

maria: I rolled one host back to v1.4.2 in the customer's pool and their calls immediately returned 200 and tenant claim parsed OK. Customer confirmed.

deploy-bot: rollback job edge-auth-proxy:v1.4.2 -> vpc-edge-2 initiated by maria at 2025-11-09T01:04:12Z.

kevin: Root cause summary for the postmortem: a change in v1.4.3 replaced header-forwarding template with a compact template that appended cookie values to existing header when cookie var was non-empty. The template used `set-header Authorization "$http_authorization, $cookie_session"` instead of conditional set/copy. When no cookie present it left header alone; when cookie present it concatenated incorrectly.

maria: Fixes: 
- Immediate: rollback vpc-edge-2 to v1.4.2 (done).
- Short: patch v1.4.3 to use conditional header set: `if ($cookie_session) { set_header Authorization $http_authorization; set_header X-Session-Cookie $cookie_session; }` — and add integration test.
- Long: expand our staging integration tests to include signed cookie headers and verify Authorization parity end-to-end.

Ajay: Also add a regression test that uses a real-length JWT + cookie values and validates runtime sees exact Authorization bytes. Put test in deploy/edge-auth-proxy CI.

sre-oncall: I'll open an incident and track SLA/customer communications. Also logging improvement: if JWT parse fails at runtime, include a hash of the header bytes (not token) so we can triage header-mangling faster without exposing secrets.

maria: Filed INC-2025-0427, alerted customer, and attached reproducer + tcpdump. Customer is happy with rollback and timeline.

kevin: Nice catch. Leaving this thread open until v1.4.3 is patched and CI tests merged. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — closing when patch is merged.
